title: B1-01 · Roots, schemes and dictionary by root

blocks.text: B1-01 · Roots, schemes and dictionary by root
Lesson overview

Level B1 begins with a tool you will use throughout the rest of the course: a dictionary organised by root. In A2, you learnt that almost every Arabic word comes from a root and a pattern (A2-01), and you recognised the derived forms (A2-18). Now you will turn that knowledge into a method: when you encounter an unfamiliar word, even without vowel marks, you will break it down layer by layer, identify its root even if a letter has disappeared or changed, find it in the dictionary and choose the meaning that fits the context. This step will help you work independently with the authentic texts in module B1.3. Two weeks.

rows: Examination A2 exceeded; root and scheme (A2-01); weak verbs (A2-15, A2-16); derived forms (A2-17, A2-18)
12–14 hours · two weeks (weeks 95–96 of the calendar), plus the EGY track-01 in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a dictionary ordered by root (Appendix C), script for speech synthesis, session with the tutor
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. break down a word, even without vowels, into proclitics, prefixes, root with scheme, desinences and pronouns
suffixes;
2. categorize the root: healthy, with hamza, doubled, assimilated, concave, defective, doubly weak,
four letters;
3. rebuild the root when a letter has fallen, stretched or changed;
4. read a dictionary entry by root: form I with imperfect vowel and maṣdar, forms II.X, names,
pluralities and parts thereof;
5. choose between several meanings the one suitable for the context;
6. translate short sentences containing words you are looking for.
Two-week plan.

6. The derived forms in research

The dictionary by root first lists the form I, then the derived forms with their number (in the dictionaries of European tradition often in Roman figures: II, III, IV...). To search for a derived verb you must therefore recognize the scheme and reduce it to the root. Review table of A2-18 (G36) and add unvoweled signals:

rows: ⁧أ⁩ initial to perfect, ⁧يُـ⁩ to the imperfect, ⁧إ⁩ in maṣdar

blocks.text: The most difficult case: form II without vowels. ⁧درس⁩ may be ⁧دَرَسَ⁩ • has studied • (I) ⁧دَرَّسَ⁩ He taught (II). The dictionary shows you both: context decides (who does the action? is there a complement in person?). In B1-17 You'll come back to this ambiguity.

The derived forms in order, with the number. 4. The names, each with his own plural. 5. Participants maṣdar of derived forms. In true dictionaries abbreviations are explained in the introduction: read it once, calmly. Root order. The dictionaries per root follow the order of the Arabic alphabet on the first radical, then on the second, then on the third: ⁧ك ت ب⁩ comes before ⁧ك ت م⁩ , which comes before ⁧ك ث ر⁩ . The roots with hamza are searched under the letter ⁧أ⁩ . Bilingual dictionaries. Not all Arabic-Italian dictionaries are sorted by root: some follow the alphabetical order of the entire word. Check in the introduction of your dictionary how entries are sorted before starting (Appendix C).
8. Choose the meaning

Many words have more meanings. The rule: identify the category (verb, name, adjective), the form, then the field of the text (cronaca, economy, school...) and choose the meaning that makes the phrase coherent.

9. Foreign words and special cases

Foreign words. ⁧تِلِفِزْيُون⁩ , ⁧كُمْبْيُوتَر⁩ , ⁧بَنْك⁩ , ⁧دِيمُقْرَاطِيَّة⁩ , ⁧بَرْنَامَج⁩ they have no Arabic root. Many dictionaries list them as if their consonants were a root ( ⁧ت ل ف ز⁩ ...), others in alphabetical order; Try both ways. Some foreign words have become rooting and produce verbs: ⁧دَبْلُومَاسِيّ⁩ , ⁧أَرْشِيف⁩ → ⁧أَرْشَفَ⁩ • to store the file. Names and places. I am not in the general dictionary: for cities and countries see ONO-03. Ancient words with root of two apparent letters. ⁧أَب⁩ "Father' means: ⁧أَخ⁩ "Brother's" ⁧يَد⁩ "hand' is the word "hand', ⁧دَم⁩ Blood (including blood) ⁧اِسْم⁩ "name' means the name of the person, ⁧اِبْن⁩ "son": they have a weak root hidden ( ⁧أ ب و⁩ , ⁧أ خ و⁩ , ⁧ي د ي⁩ , ⁧د م و⁩ , ⁧س م و⁩ , ⁧ب ن ي⁩ ). The plural often shows it: ⁧آبَاء⁩ , ⁧إِخْوَة⁩ , ⁧أَيْدٍ⁩ , ⁧دِمَاء⁩ , ⁧أَسْمَاء⁩ , ⁧أَبْنَاء⁩ .
10. Pronunciation

Read new words without vowels. Once you find the pattern, you already know how to pronounce the word: ⁧اِسْتِقْبَال⁩ Following ⁧اِسْتِفْعَال⁩ ( istiqbāl), ⁧مُسْتَشْفَيَات⁩ Following the passive participle of X with ⁧ـات⁩ ( mustašfayāt). Before reading a long word aloud, divide it into syllables according to the scheme: is-tiq-bāl, mus-taš-fa-yāt. The accent. In the long words the accent falls on the long syllable closest to the end, without going beyond the third last: istiqBĀL, mustašfaYĀT, maʿLŪmāt. Do not put the accent on the first syllable as in many Italian words.
